## Body

PASS-WITH-NOTES — static performance, PR #281 / F232, exact head ed493731a221dc57a17811962203ee07ff925429.

No blocking performance finding. Source review only; no build, test, deployment or live measurement performed by this seat.

Let R be retry-eligible errored rows and N the live pending spawned Codex rows (R <= N). PROBE_RETRIES=3 permits three additional probes, four including the original, on the existing default 5-second binder cadence. Under an unchanged lockset, exhaustion stops further probes; new thread starts remain existing external triggers.

[INFERENCE] Static cost envelope:

| Accounting scope | Added per row, three retries | Added per eligible 5-second tick | Offered rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Requested persistent pane-error test model: two counted Facts operations/probe | 6 (8 including original) | 2R | 0.4R/s |
| Conservative production read-error envelope: recorded launch-site invocations, not descendant PID births | <=15 | <=5R | <=R/s |

The second envelope allows one lsof plus two tmux reads, each with at most one control-start and one fallback-fork invocation; a later proc_start-error path instead uses at most four such invocations. A successful retry also performs existing registration work, outside this read-error envelope. At N=80, the requested two-operation model offers at most 160/tick (32/s) for three retry ticks, then zero retry demand without a new trigger.

Facts::launches is mocked stage accounting, not OS measurement: a successful probe visits three Facts stages. Actual macOS Query::Busy costs one existing /usr/sbin/lsof and zero tmux launches while Busy persists; prolonged contention can enter #280's existing fallback. Live proc_start is normally in-process, with existing absolute /bin/ps fallback. Therefore six is not a universal OS-launch ceiling.

Memory: failures retains only IDs failed in the last completed pass, at most N entries; transient failed is also O(N). Success/non-error results, disappearance and the quiet pass after exhaustion prune entries. No historical accumulation or fixed global row cap. retain uses Vec::contains: worst O(R_previous * R_current) comparisons, plus BTreeMap updates.

No new recurring loop, timer, task or launch site. There are new in-process retain/update passes inside the existing binder invocation. crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs is unchanged; existing lsof, tmux and ps sites remain recorded. References: codex_bind.rs:159-185,238-295,301-377; codex_bind_tests.rs:86-110,267-289; lib.rs:797-815; tmux/lib.rs:350-355,469-484,886-908; tmux/control.rs:301-407; harnesses/codex.rs:80-116; harnesses/proc.rs:88-105,287-297.

Correctness scope remains with the independent reviewer: registration Runtime errors are currently converted to Ok(false), and overlapping thread starts do not explicitly reset the failure counter. Both were reported; this performance verdict is not ship acceptance.
